newsitem.title: BRAZIL: U.S. funds want to buy Banespa - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. funds want to buy Banespa - paper.

text.p: Government sources say Brazilian investors with links to U.S. investment funds are interested in buying up indebted Sao Paulo state bank Banespa, a financial newspaper reported.
The federal government and Sao Paulo state are finalizing details on a debt restructuring deal sealed early this year.

Gazeta Mercantil said the government was holding talks on the Banespa sale with a group of Brazilian investors who have ties to the private U.S. investment partnership Texas Pacific Group, whose principals include David Bonderman.

The Brazilians are associates of Bonderman in the private equity fund Newbridge Latin America, which has 400 million reais ($377.4 million) to invest in Brazilian and other Latin American companies, Gazeta said.

Government sources said the Banespa sale could amount to 800 million reais ($754.7 million), which would be paid by the funds administered by Bonderman and his American associates, according to Gazeta.
Bonderman would not head the bank should the deal come through, but a group of professionally qualified Brazilian directors would take over management of the bank, Gazeta said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
